sentences.text: Leucoraja is a genus of hardnose skates belonging to the family Rajidae, and its members are commonly known as rough skates.
There are currently 15 recognized species within this genus.
The genus Leucoraja was described by Malm in 1877.
The type species of the genus Leucoraja is Raja fullonica, which was originally described by Linnaeus in 1758.
Leucoraja circularis, known as the sandy ray, was described by Couch in 1838.
Leucoraja compagnoi, known as the tigertail skate, was described by Stehmann in 1995.
Leucoraja elaineae was described by Ebert and Leslie in 2019.
Leucoraja erinaceus, known as the little skate, was described by Mitchill in 1825.
Leucoraja fullonica, known as the shagreen skate, was described by Linnaeus in 1758.
Leucoraja garmani, known as the rosette skate, was described by Whitley in 1939.
Leucoraja lentiginosa, known as the freckled skate, was described by Bigelow and Schroeder in 1951.
Leucoraja leucosticta, known as the whitedappled skate, was described by Stehmann in 1971.
Leucoraja longirostris, known as the brown longnose skate, was described by Weigmann, Stehmann, Séret, and Ishihara in 2024.
Leucoraja melitensis, known as the Maltese skate, was described by R. S. Clark in 1926.
Leucoraja naevus, known as the cuckoo skate, was described by J. P. Müller and Henle in 1841.
Leucoraja ocellata, known as the winter skate, was described by Mitchill in 1815.
Leucoraja pristispina, known as the sawback skate, was described by Last, Stehmann, and Séret in 2008.
Leucoraja wallacei, known as the yellow-spotted skate, was described by Hulley in 1970.
Leucoraja yucatanensis, known as the Yucatán skate, was described by Bigelow and Schroeder in 1950.
Leucoraja caribbaea, known as the Maya skate, is a synonym valid as Leucoraja garmani.
Leucoraja virginica, known as the Virginia skate, is a synonym valid as Leucoraja garmani.
Leucoraja is a genus of fish in the family Rajidae, the order Rajiformes, and the class Chondrichthyes.
The genus is found in the Atlantic, Mediterranean, south-western Indian Ocean, and Australia.
